Subject: Acme POC trial integration - success criteria & next steps

Hi Sam — great to meet you and Lina today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed plan from our side so we have alignment before the trial starts next week.

Summary of what we heard from Acme
- Primary use case: realtime assistant in internal support portal (short-context Q&A + tool calls to internal search)
- Target latency: <= 250ms p95 for token streaming in production
- Volume during trial: ~50 concurrent sessions, avg 20 messages/session

Proposed success criteria (please confirm or edit)
1) Functional: Assistant returns accurate answer for 80% of a curated 50-prompt evaluation set (we'll run evals together)
2) Performance: Inference latency p95 <= 250ms for streaming path under expected trial load
3) Integration: SDK-based integration that supports streaming and tool calling within your frontend by the end of the trial
4) Security/compliance: Access to SOC 2 Type II report and data isolation for logs during the trial

Attached: acme_eval_plan.xlsx — includes evaluation prompts, owners, and proposed go/no-go criteria.

Next steps / owners (proposed)
- Acme: Lina (engineering lead) to provision a dev environment and provide a point-of-contact for keys and network questions (owner: Lina)
- Redwood: Marcus (solutions engineer) to deliver integration checklist and sample code; Marissa to coordinate schedule and commercial items (owners: Marcus + Marissa)
- Sync: Weekly 30-min integration stand starting Thursday 2026-03-26, invite to follow

Can you confirm the success criteria and timeline (targeting a decision by 2026-04-15)? If anything above needs to change I can update the plan.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,

Hi Lina/Sam — quick tech kickoff note and concrete items Marcus will deliver for the dev sync on Mon 3/29. High-level implementation guidance below.

1) SDK & quickstart
- Python SDK: pip install redwood-client==1.3.0
- JS SDK: npm install @redwood/inference@^1.3.0
- Config: use dev API key (scope: generate, embeddings, tool_call). Keys are per-environment.

2) Endpoints & patterns
- Non-streaming: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (JSON: {model, input, max_tokens})
- Streaming: Websocket/SSE at wss://stream.redwood.ai/v1/stream (recommended for UI; delivers incremental tokens and token-level timings)
- Tool calling: include tools schema in the call ("tools": [{"name":"internal_search","schema":{...}}]); Redwood will return a tool_call object if the model invokes a tool.

3) Example (Python streaming snippet)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<DEV_KEY>")
with client.stream(model="redwood-llama-13b", input="Find latest instructions for refund policy") as stream:
    for event in stream:
        if event.type == "token":
            print(event.token, end="")
        elif event.type == "tool_call":
            # call your internal search API with event.payload
            pass

4) Performance tips
- Enable prefix caching for repeated system messages; this reduces token compute for cold requests
- Use batching for backend-heavy workflows (we'll advise batch sizes after we see traffic shape)
- For trial, keep sequence length trimmed to the active context (recommended 1024 tokens) to meet the 250ms p95 target

5) Observability & toggles
- We'll provide a per-route dashboard for tokens, latency, and model version; enable debug logs for first 48 hours only
- Suggested fallbacks: model-variant fallback to a smaller quantized model if p95 spikes above 350ms

6) Files I'm attaching to help the dev team:
- acme_sample_code_snippets.txt (contains sample curl/python/js commands and JSON schema examples)
- redwood-integration-checklist.pdf (detailed step checklist)

If Lina's team can share a test endpoint for the internal search, we'll include the tool schema example in the first sync. Happy to hop on a 30-min screen share during the 3/29 meetup and pair on the streaming integration.

--
